subject: Re: PayRide integration — auth playbook and next milestones
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Alan Cho <alan@payride.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T14:05:00-08:00
Subject: PayRide demo follow-up — proposed auth playbook and asks

Alan — great to meet you and the PayRide team today. Thanks for walking through the call flows and the high-level privacy requirements. This thread is a quick recap plus proposed next steps so we have a shared checklist for the engineering and security teams.

Summary (short):
- Demo covered routing, streaming results, embeddings for rider matching, and tool-calling for live pricing.
- Primary open item: authentication model and key management for both Hosted API and Private (VPC) deploys. PayRide needs clear guidance on tokens, rotation, and service accounts.

Proposed auth playbook (high level):
1) Prod integration path: service-account JWTs + short-lived API tokens. We recommend Minted short-lived tokens (1h) for app-level calls, backed by a service account that performs minting.
2) Key rotation: automated rotation every 30 days for long-term keys; short-lived tokens rotated per issuance. We will provide a sample rotation script and a webhook-based revocation endpoint.
3) OAuth option: If you prefer user-delegated access for certain admin actions (ex: telemetry exports), we can support OAuth 2.0 with JWT assertion for server-to-server flows.
4) RBAC and per-route tokens: we suggest a scoped token model so tokens grant limited route access (generation vs embeddings vs admin).
5) Compliance evidence: we can share our KMS integration guide and SOC snippets with your security team.

Concrete asks from PayRide (please comment inline):
- Which authentication pattern do you prefer for "rider-matching" service: service-account minted tokens vs static API key?
- Do you require integration with your internal KMS/HSM for key storage?
- Any SSO/SCIM needs for onboarding developer accounts?

Attachments: redwood-auth-arch-v1.png (arch diagram), payride-oauth-proposal.docx (draft OAuth flow).

Next steps (my proposal):
- Alan + PayRide Security to confirm preferred pattern by EOD Monday 2026-11-16.
- Rishi will produce an implementation checklist and sample token-minting script by 11/18.
- Follow-up technical session (30–45m) week of 11/22 to walk through code samples and edge cases (KV cache, token reuse).

Thanks — I’ve put the HubSpot deal link here and will update the next milestones once we agree on the auth pattern.

Cheers,
Monica

From: Alan Cho <alan@payride.io>

Date: 2026-11-15T17:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: PayRide demo follow-up — proposed auth playbook and asks

Thanks, Monica — great demo and appreciate the clear playbook. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) For rider-matching we prefer short-lived tokens minted by a service account (that aligns with our threat model). We want tokens scoped to embeddings & reranking endpoints only.
2) KMS: we will want integration with our internal AWS KMS for root key wrapping. Can Redwood support using an external KMS/HSM for private deployments?
3) Rotation cadence: 30-day rotation for root keys sounds fine. For the short-lived tokens, can we issue with 15m TTL for backend-to-backend calls (we can extend later if necessary)?
4) Auditing: security team asked whether Redwood can log token issuer and token id for each request (audit fields) — we need that retained for 180 days.

Open question: Do you support JWT-based assertion (signed by our KMS) to mint Redwood tokens, or would it require us to keep a private key in Redwood? We prefer not to store long-lived private keys outside our environment.

If you can confirm the KMS/HSM flow and the JWT assertion model, we'll be comfortable moving forward with the PoC.

—Alan
Director, Platform Engineering | PayRide
alan@payride.io
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Alan Cho <alan@payride.io>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T19:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: PayRide demo follow-up — proposed auth playbook and asks

Alan — quick technical replies inline.

On KMS/HSM: yes — for Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and HSM-backed wrapping. The service-account private keys do not need to be stored in Redwood for private installs; we can accept JWT assertions signed by your KMS. For Hosted, we can implement a hybrid model where you hold the master wrapping key in your KMS and we perform ephemeral wrapping in our environment using CMEK.

On JWT assertion: we support the JWT assertion grant flow. Recommended pattern:
- PayRide signs a short-lived JWT using a key material stored in your KMS (asymmetric).
- Redwood validates the JWT assertion, then issues a short-lived Redwood API token with scoped permissions.
- Token issued for 15m TTL (configurable per client); refresh via same assertion endpoint.

On rotation and revocation:
- Root keys: rotate in your KMS per your schedule; Redwood will accept the new public key via a key-registration endpoint.
- Token revocation: we provide an immediate token revocation endpoint and an optional webhook to notify your services when a token is revoked.

On auditing: we will include per-request headers for token_id and issuer and can push logs to your SIEM via secure syslog or S3 (encrypted). We can provide 180-day retention as an add-on or via Private contract.

I'll attach a quick auth-arch diagram and a sample minting script (pseudo) to the Drive link Monica provided. Happy to demo the JWT assertion flow in the follow-up session.

Rishi
Senior Applied ML Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

> Alan — yes, we can validate JWTs signed by your KMS and avoid storing private keys in Redwood for Private customers. For Hosted customers we can also offer a hybrid CMEK pattern (details in attachment).

Alan — thanks for the quick replies and the clarifications above.

Recap of decisions so far:
- Pattern agreed (for PoC): JWT assertion signed by PayRide KMS -> Redwood token (15m TTL) scoped to embeddings & rerank endpoints.
- KMS: PayRide will use AWS KMS for root key wrapping; Redwood will accept public-key registration and validate JWT assertions.
- Auditing: Redwood will emit token_id + issuer headers and can deliver logs to your S3 bucket with 180-day retention (we will include this as a line item in the PoC SOW).

Action items assigned:
- PayRide (Alan / Security): share a sample public key and desired token scope definitions by 2026-11-18. (Alan)
- Redwood (Rishi): share sample minting script + minimal server implementation for validating JWT assertions by 2026-11-18. (Rishi)
- Monica: schedule a 30m technical demo for 2026-11-23 — invite: Alan, PayRide Security, Rishi, Marissa.

I’ve updated HubSpot (deal PR-2026-0997) with these milestones and added the PoC SOW draft. I'll also attach the architecture PNG in Drive. If that looks right, we can finalize the PoC SOW and provide a limited-time test key for PayRide to validate flows.

Available times for the demo: 11/23 at 10:00 PT or 11/24 at 11:00 PT — which works best for you?

Thanks — looking forward to moving this to PoC.
